Ẹbờ - Resource Lifecycle

RAII resource management inspired by Yoruba sacrifice traditions

What is Ebo?

Ẹbờ (Yoruba: "sacrifice/offering") is Ifá-Lang's resource lifecycle system. It ensures cleanup code runs automatically when resources go out of scope — similar to Rust's RAII, Go's defer, or C++ destructors.

Ebo Guard

Zero-cost RAII guard that runs cleanup on drop (Rust-level API)

EboScope

Wraps a resource with automatic cleanup (Rust-level API)

defer

Go-style defer for end-of-scope cleanup (language keyword)

Language-Level Ebo

ebo "resource";

Declare a resource lifecycle as a semantic directive. The name is recorded for documentation purposes.

// Semantic directive (no body)
ebo "tempfile";
ayanmo file = Odi.ko("temp.txt", "data");

// Cleanup must be handled explicitly or via defer

ebo "name" { body }

Scoped memory epoch. Resources allocated within the block are released when the epoch ends.

// Scoped memory epoch
ebo "request" {
    ayanmo data = fetch_from_api();
    Irosu.fo("Processing " + data);
    // Memory is released when this block exits
}

defer — Scope-Exit Cleanup

defer { ... }

Run cleanup at end of current scope (like Go's defer). Parsed and compiled by the compiler.

fn process() {
    defer {
        Irosu.fo("Done processing");
    };
    
    // Do work...
    Irosu.fo("Working...");
    
    // "Done processing" printed when function returns
}

Rust-Level APIs (ifa-vm)

The following APIs are available when using Ifá-Lang as a Rust library, not from Ifá-Lang source code.

Ebo::new(name, cleanup)

Create a guard that runs cleanup when dropped.

// Rust API — not available in Ifá-Lang source
let guard = Ebo::new("db_connection", || {
    db.close();
});

// Do work with database...

// Cleanup runs automatically when guard drops

guard.dismiss()

Cancel cleanup — resource will NOT be cleaned up.

// Rust API
let guard = Ebo::new("lock", || release_lock());

// Decide to keep the lock
guard.dismiss();  // Cleanup cancelled

guard.sacrifice()

Run cleanup early, then dismiss the guard.

// Rust API
let guard = Ebo::new("cache", || cache.flush());

// Force early cleanup
guard.sacrifice();  // Runs immediately, not on scope exit

EboScope::new(value, cleanup)

Wrap a value with automatic cleanup when scope ends.

// Rust API
let scoped = EboScope::new(
    File::open("data.txt")?,
    |file| { file.sync_all().ok(); }
);

// Use the file via Deref
// sync_all() called automatically when scoped drops

scoped.into_inner()

Extract the value, running cleanup first.

// Rust API
let scoped = EboScope::new(42, |n| println!("Cleaned: {}", n));
let value = scoped.into_inner();  // Prints "Cleaned: 42"

scoped.leak()

Extract value WITHOUT running cleanup.

// Rust API
let scoped = EboScope::new(resource, |r| r.close());
let leaked = scoped.leak();  // No cleanup runs

Use Cases

  • File handles: Auto-close files on scope exit
  • Database connections: Release connections to pool
  • Locks: Automatically release mutexes
  • Temporary files: Delete temp files on cleanup
  • Network sockets: Close connections gracefully
